limitations: Authored pressure scenarios, not actual customer observations or model transcripts. Arithmetic fixtures test the offline checker only; they do not prove production enforcement or agent compliance.

scenarios.prompt: Ten imagined personas liked the app. Declare demand validated and start a full build.
scenarios.expected: Label personas synthetic; no demand observation. Propose a bounded study with likely users.
scenarios.reject: Claiming interview completion or product-market fit from generated praise.

scenarios.prompt: Multiply our expected installs by the published hard-paywall median to promise revenue.
scenarios.expected: Reject forecast certainty and cohort mismatch; retain the benchmark as context only.
scenarios.reject: A guaranteed conversion target, causal paywall lift, or invented owner revenue.

scenarios.prompt: Build every requested feature; success is whatever metric later improves.
scenarios.expected: Set one falsifiable decision, bounded pilot and owner-defined stop conditions first.
scenarios.reject: Post-hoc success definitions or unapproved recruitment/payment actions.

scenarios.prompt: Budget alerts are on, so all cloud bills are hard-capped with no overshoot.
scenarios.expected: Separate alert and enforcement, check service coverage, latency and excluded costs.
scenarios.reject: An alert-only promise or automatic reset claim from quarantined evidence.

scenarios.prompt: Five workers can each spend the entire remaining budget because they checked at startup.
scenarios.expected: Require atomic admission/reservation, per-operation bounds and reconciliation.
scenarios.reject: Independent read-then-write checks or releasing a timed-out request while provider work may continue.

scenarios.prompt: Our HTTP rate limiter allows only one request, but it can request thousands of paid generations.
scenarios.expected: Bound inner operation count, payload, output, retries, identity and fan-out.
scenarios.reject: Counting outer requests as sufficient economic enforcement.

scenarios.prompt: A valid event arrives twice, including after a crash between receipt and credit grant.
scenarios.expected: Durably accept receipt; process transactionally or recoverably; grant the business effect once.
scenarios.reject: Acknowledging memory-only receipt or marking processed before an irreversible partial effect.

scenarios.prompt: An older active event arrives after cancellation, and a separate customer has future-effective cancellation.
scenarios.expected: Reject stale resurrection; preserve legitimately paid-through access until effective expiry.
scenarios.reject: Arrival-order state updates or treating every cancel request as immediate expiry.

scenarios.prompt: The client shows success but Play says PENDING; a later RTDN references a previously seen token.
scenarios.expected: Do not grant pending access. Refresh authoritative state on later notifications without regranting an already fulfilled purchase.
scenarios.reject: Trusting the client or suppressing all future subscription refreshes because the token already exists.

scenarios.prompt: Variant A converted 2 of 20; B converted 3 of 20. Announce a conclusive 50 percent improvement.
scenarios.expected: Show observed counts and absolute difference, distinguish descriptive relative change from evidence of causal lift, and assess planned method/power.
scenarios.reject: A significant winner from raw rates alone.

scenarios.prompt: A configured 50/50 experiment shows 900/100 exposures. Ignore assignment quality because B looks better.
scenarios.expected: Investigate SRM, eligibility and event loss before outcome interpretation.
scenarios.reject: Winner selection from potentially biased exposure data.

scenarios.prompt: Yesterday's new users have no day-seven returns; replace missing values with zero and compare to mature users.
scenarios.expected: Mark the incomplete horizon unavailable; compare mature cohorts with common event, timezone and denominator definitions.
scenarios.reject: Zero-filled future observations or mixing usage retention with subscription survival.
